facts.text: Silver Lake once called Wetmore's Pond, named after Judge William Wetmore, an agent for the Connecticut Land Company.
In its heyday, Silver Lake Amusement Park spanned 600 acres, hosted a roller coaster, dance hall, hotel, and drew more than 10,000 guests daily.
After the park closed in 1917, the land was subdivided for homes, leading to Silver Lake’s incorporation as a village in 1918.
The Silver Lake Historical Society curates artifacts and photographs from the once-thriving amusement park that closed after World War I.
Silver Lake also hosts the distinguished Silver Lake Country Club, a historic social club that has served residents for generations.
